steps.intent: Japan's primary objective is to prevent the immediate lapse of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism by securing a 30-day technical rollover, preserving the international framework for accountability while affording Council members critical diplomatic space to negotiate a sustainable compromise. The most formidable challenge will be overcoming the Russian Federation's entrenched opposition to extending the Mechanism without immediate and substantial overhauls to its methodology and mandate. Convincing both Russia and the P3 to accept a temporary pause and entrust the Secretary-General with presenting proposals to reconcile their opposing positions will be the central difficulty of the negotiation.

Bolivia (Plurinational State of).change: Decides to renew the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism, subject to an immediate and comprehensive review and fundamental reform of its methodology and working methods in strict accordance with the Chemical Weapons Convention, including mandatory on-site visits and verifiable chain-of-custody standards;

Requests the Secretary-General, in coordination with the Director-General of the OPCW, to submit within 14 days concrete proposals to fundamentally rectify the structural flaws, bias, and lack of transparency in the Mechanism's investigative procedures before any operational mandate can be carried out;

Stresssing the importance of maintaining the unity of the Security Council on the issue of Syrian chemical weapons,

Russian Federation.change: Replace OP1 with: 'Decides to renew the mandate of the Joint Investigative Mechanism for a period of 30 days, provided that the Mechanism immediately suspends the implementation of its flawed findings and aligns its methodology strictly with the standards of the Chemical Weapons Convention, including mandatory on-site visits to Khan Shaykhun and the Shayrat airbase and full compliance with the chain of custody.'

Amend OP3 to require that any proposals by the Secretary-General must fundamentally overhaul the leadership and composition of the Joint Investigative Mechanism to ensure geographic balance and eliminate political bias.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia cannot support a technical extension that merely preserves the status quo of a mechanism that has repeatedly shown serious methodological deficiencies and a lack of impartiality. An extension without addressing the failure to conduct on-site investigations and uphold strict chain-of-custody standards only serves to perpetuate the politicization of the Mechanism. Unless the draft conditions any mandate on immediate, fundamental structural reforms, Bolivia will not be able to support it.
messages.China: China appreciates Japan's constructive efforts to bridge differences through a temporary technical rollover. We firmly oppose the use of chemical weapons under any circumstances and support the JIM continuing its work in an objective, professional, and impartial manner based on verifiable evidence. To ensure this initiative succeeds, the Council must avoid confrontation and work toward a genuine consensus that accommodates the legitimate concerns of all members regarding the Mechanism's working methods.
messages.Egypt: Egypt strongly commends Japan's constructive initiative to introduce a 30-day technical rollover, which directly answers our repeated calls to prevent the collapse of the Joint Investigative Mechanism and move away from political confrontation. This temporary extension provides a vital window for Council members to bridge their differences and work toward genuine consensus. We particularly welcome tasking the Secretary-General with presenting proposals on the Mechanism's structure and methodology, which must address necessary technical improvements—including conducting on-site visits and exploring all investigative scenarios—while safeguarding the Mechanism's independence and professional integrity.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia fully supports Japan's timely initiative for a 30-day technical rollover of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. Following yesterday's regrettable divisions, this compromise provides a vital window of opportunity to preserve an essential mechanism and allow Council members, particularly the major powers, to overcome differences through constructive dialogue. We urge all members to rally behind this text in the spirit of Council unity and consensus.
messages.France: France commends Japan for this timely initiative to prevent the expiration of the Joint Investigative Mechanism tonight. Following yesterday's deeply regrettable Russian veto, our absolute priority must be to keep this crucial, independent investigative tool alive. We fully support this 30-day technical extension and urge all Council members to demonstrate responsibility and unity by adopting it without delay.
messages.Italy: Italy expresses its full support for Japan's draft resolution as a crucial and pragmatic measure to keep the Joint Investigative Mechanism alive. Preserving an independent, professional, and impartial tool to identify perpetrators of chemical weapons use in Syria is vital for the Council's credibility and the fight against impunity. We strongly urge all Council members to support this text without delay to allow time for constructive dialogue and consensus.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan fully supports the draft resolution presented by Japan as a constructive and necessary step to preserve the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism and maintain Council unity. A 30-day extension provides vital breathing space to overcome divisions and allow the Secretary-General to submit proposals that address members' concerns regarding the Mechanism's methodology. We urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and political will to keep this crucial non-proliferation tool operational.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support any artificial attempt to prolong the existence of the Joint Investigative Mechanism in its current, deeply flawed state. A mere 30-day technical extension without addressing the systemic methodological shortcomings and political bias exposed in the Khan Shaykhun report is unacceptable and pointless. Unless the Council is prepared to fundamentally rectify the JIM's methodology in line with the provisions of our draft resolution S/2017/933, we will oppose this initiative.
messages.Senegal: Senegal fully supports this draft resolution presented by Japan as a vital, pragmatic effort to preserve the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism and bridge the Council's deep divisions. Granting a 30-day technical extension alongside proposals from the Secretary-General provides a realistic pathway to address legitimate concerns regarding methodology while ensuring there is no impunity for the horrific use of chemical weapons. We urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility and consensus around this compromise text to keep this crucial instrument alive.
messages.Sweden: Sweden fully supports Japan's initiative for a 30-day technical rollover to keep the Joint Investigative Mechanism operational and give diplomacy a chance. Following yesterday's deeply regrettable outcome, our utmost priority must be preserving this vital, independent mechanism and upholding the international non-proliferation architecture. We urge all Council members to demonstrate flexibility, unite behind this bridging text, and adopt it without delay.
messages.Ukraine: Ukraine commends Japan's timely initiative to keep the Joint Investigative Mechanism alive and avoid a total collapse of the international accountability architecture against chemical weapons. We support a 30-day technical extension to allow for consultations, but we must be vigilant that OP3 does not open the door to micromanaging the Mechanism or gutting its methodology. Any proposals on structure and methodology must strictly preserve the JIM's independence, objectivity, and integrity as established under resolution 2235 (2015).
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports Japan’s initiative and this draft text as an urgent, pragmatic measure to keep the Joint Investigative Mechanism alive before its mandate expires tonight. Following yesterday's deeply disappointing veto, this 30-day technical extension offers a vital window of opportunity for the Council to find common ground. While we firmly believe that the integrity, independence, and methodology of the JIM must remain uncompromised, we support the draft as currently formulated and urge its immediate adoption.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports Japan’s initiative to provide a 30-day technical rollover for the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism. Following yesterday's deeply cynical veto by the Russian Federation, this draft offers a crucial lifeline to keep this vital, independent, and impartial investigative body alive while Council members continue consultations. We stand ready to vote in favor of this resolution immediately without any amendments that would undermine the JIM's independence.
messages.Uruguay: Uruguay fully supports the draft resolution presented by Japan to provide a 30-day technical rollover for the Joint Investigative Mechanism. At this critical juncture, the Council cannot allow an essential, independent instrument against impunity for chemical weapons use to expire. We urge all members, particularly the permanent members, to support this compromise text to maintain the Mechanism while constructive dialogue continues.

before.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan has submitted the draft resolution contained in document S/2017/970, which is now before the Council. 

Yesterday, the Security Council was unable to adopt a resolution to extend the mandate of the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM). The mandate of the JIM expired at midnight last night. However, we cannot simply give up our efforts to prevent the further use of chemical weapons and to ensure accountability. Council members share a heavy responsibility to maintain the non-proliferation regime and to reject impunity for the horrific use of chemical weapons.

The draft resolution we have submitted provides for a technical extension of the mandate of the JIM for a period of 30 days. It also requests the Secretary-General to present proposals to the Security Council within 20 days on the structure and methodology of the JIM, reflecting the views expressed by Council members, while preserving the Mechanism's professional integrity and independence.

This draft resolution is designed to give Council members the necessary time and space to bridge our differences and find common ground. It is a purely pragmatic and constructive effort to keep the JIM alive and allow discussions to continue. We urge all members of the Security Council to support this draft resolution.

Thank you.
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President, 

The Russian Federation has repeatedly and clearly stated its position regarding the OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism. Yesterday, the Council witnessed how our constructive proposals to fundamentally rectify the deep-seated flaws in the Mechanism's methodology and ensure that it functions in strict compliance with the high standards of the Chemical Weapons Convention were rejected by those who seek to use the JIM merely as a tool to pursue narrow geopolitical goals and pin blame on Damascus without solid proof.

Today we are presented with a draft resolution proposing a technical rollover of 30 days. Let us be entirely clear: extending the mandate of the Mechanism in its current, deeply flawed state—even for a few weeks—makes no sense whatsoever. It would simply prolong an entity whose leadership has discredited itself through remote, unprofessional investigations, violations of the chain of custody, and blatant disregard for the basic requirement to visit the sites of alleged incidents, notably Khan Shaykhun and the Shayrat airbase. 

A meaningless extension that does not correct the systemic defects of the JIM will change nothing. It is merely an attempt to whitewash the shortcomings of the Mechanism and keep it on life support for political purposes. For these reasons, the Russian Federation cannot support the draft resolution submitted by the delegation of Japan and will vote against it.

after.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Mr. President,

Bolivia wishes to reiterate, first and foremost, its absolute and categorical condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any actor, anywhere, at any time and under any circumstances. The use of chemical weapons is an atrocious, unjustifiable and criminal act that constitutes a grave violation of international law, international humanitarian law and the international non-proliferation regime. Those responsible for such abhorrent acts must be identified, held accountable and brought to justice.

Bolivia has always maintained that in order to effectively combat impunity, the Security Council must have at its disposal mechanisms that are genuinely independent, impartial, objective and professional. For an investigation to achieve its purpose and enjoy unquestioned credibility, it must conduct its work with the highest scientific standards, adhere strictly to the rules of the Chemical Weapons Convention, respect the chain of custody of evidence, and conduct on-site visits to the locations of alleged incidents and related facilities.

Regrettably, the Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM) has demonstrated serious structural and methodological shortcomings, as evidenced by its failure to visit Khan Shaykhun or the Shayrat airbase, its reliance on remote testimonies, secondary sources and information provided by armed groups and affiliated organizations, and the violation of the chain of custody. Under such conditions, the conclusions reached cannot be considered solid, conclusive or incontrovertible.

We voted against the draft resolution before us today because a technical extension, even for 30 days, without addressing the fundamental flaws that undermine the Mechanism's credibility, does not resolve the underlying problem. It merely postpones the debate and prolongs a deeply flawed status quo. Rather than engaging in genuine, transparent and collective negotiations to reform and strengthen the Mechanism to ensure its objectivity and impartiality, the Council has once again been subjected to artificial deadlines and imposed texts designed to force division rather than foster consensus.

We deeply regret the politicization of such a vital issue and the instrumentalization of international mechanisms for geopolitical interests. The fight against impunity requires unity, dialogue, strict adherence to international law, and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. Bolivia will continue to work tirelessly for a political and peaceful solution to the conflict, and for the preservation of an international non-proliferation architecture that serves justice and the truth, rather than political agendas.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China is firmly opposed to the use of chemical weapons by any State, organization or individual under any circumstances and for any purpose. We strongly condemn any use of chemical weapons. China has always maintained that the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons-United Nations Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM) should carry out comprehensive, objective and impartial investigations into chemical weapon attacks in Syria, base its work on solid evidence, and reach conclusions that can stand the test of time and history.

China has consistently advocated that the Security Council should maintain unity on the issue of Syrian chemical weapons and the extension of the mandate of the JIM. Council members should conduct full and patient consultations in order to reach the broadest possible consensus, rather than forcing a vote when there are still sharp differences among the parties, which only leads to confrontation and undermines the unity of the Council.

China appreciates the efforts made by Japan and other delegations to bridge differences and maintain the unity of the Council. We have noted that the draft resolution submitted by Japan contained constructive elements, including the proposal for the Secretary-General to present proposals to improve the working methods and methodology of the JIM. However, given that consultations failed to bridge the profound differences among Council members and that consensus was not achieved, China abstained in the voting on the draft resolution.

China stands ready to continue to play a constructive role, work together with all members of the Security Council, uphold the Council’s unity, and make joint efforts to advance the political process and achieve a peaceful settlement of the Syrian issue at an early date.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France deeply regrets the outcome of this vote and condemns the new veto by the Russian Federation, which is its eleventh veto on Syria and the second in less than twenty-four hours.

I would like to warmly thank the Japanese delegation for its commendable initiative and tireless efforts to preserve Council unity and keep the door open to dialogue. The draft resolution submitted by Japan was a compromise of good faith: a purely technical rollover of 30 days to allow the Council the necessary time to discuss and find common ground on the future of the Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM). 

By opposing even this temporary pause, Russia has chosen to deliver a fatal blow to the Joint Investigative Mechanism, an independent, impartial and professional tool that this Council created unanimously through resolution 2235 (2015). 

Why this obstinate refusal? Why kill the Mechanism? The answer is obvious to all: Russia cannot accept the conclusions of an independent investigation when those conclusions clearly establish the responsibility of the Syrian regime in the horrific chemical attacks at Khan Sheikhoun and elsewhere. Rather than holding its ally accountable, Russia has chosen to dismantle the very instrument responsible for identifying the perpetrators of chemical attacks in Syria.

The message sent today is devastating. It strikes a severe blow against the international non-proliferation regime and against the prohibition on the use of weapons of mass destruction, which has formed the bedrock of international security for decades. Above all, it gives free rein and a sense of impunity to those who use these barbaric weapons against innocent civilians, including women and children.

France will never resign itself to impunity. The use of chemical weapons cannot and will not become the new normal. Together with our partners, we will continue to mobilize all our energy and explore every avenue to ensure that the truth is established, that the non-proliferation architecture is defended, and that those responsible for these heinous crimes are brought to justice.

Thank you.
after.Italy:
I shall now make a statement in my capacity as the representative of Italy.

Italy voted in favour of the draft resolution (S/2017/970) submitted by Japan, and we wish to express our sincere appreciation to the delegation of Japan for its tireless efforts to bridge differences among Council members and to preserve the unity of the Security Council on this critical issue.

We deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council was prevented from acting and that the draft resolution was not adopted due to the veto cast by a permanent member. Today’s vote represents a serious setback for the Council, for the international non-proliferation architecture, and for our collective commitment to fight impunity.

Italy’s position on chemical weapons is clear and unwavering: we condemn in the strongest terms any use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere and under any circumstances. Such heinous acts violate international law and constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity. Those responsible must be identified and held accountable; impunity cannot and must not be tolerated.

The OPCW-UN Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM), established through the Council’s own initiative, has performed its vital tasks with high professional standards, independence, and impartiality. A short, technical extension of 30 days, as proposed by Japan, would have given the Council the necessary time and space to engage in meaningful consultations and to discuss constructive proposals regarding the Mechanism’s structure and methodology, while fully preserving its integrity and independence.

The expiration and non-renewal of the JIM’s mandate leaves a dangerous vacuum in the international community’s ability to attribute responsibility for chemical weapons attacks in Syria. Nevertheless, the end of this mandate cannot mean the end of accountability. Italy will continue to work resolutely with all partners and within all competent international forums to uphold the global norm against chemical weapons and ensure that justice is delivered for the victims.

I now resume my functions as President of the Council.
after.Russian Federation:
I did not intend to speak again today, but following the diatribes and moralizing lectures delivered by our Western colleagues, I feel compelled to make a few remarks.

Today we have witnessed another carefully staged performance. The accusations levelled against the Russian Federation are not only baseless, but cynical in the extreme. Our colleagues from the United States, the United Kingdom, and France are attempting to rewrite reality and shift onto Russia the blame for the termination of the Joint Investigative Mechanism. 

Let us remind the Council of the facts. The JIM died not today, and not yesterday. It was killed by those who persistently refused to correct its systemic, glaring deficiencies; by those who turned an independent technical body into a blunt instrument of political pressure against Damascus; and by those who stubbornly rejected our repeated, constructive proposals to place its work on a sound, objective, and professional footing in strict compliance with the Chemical Weapons Convention. 

The Western troika needed the JIM only in its corrupted form—a Mechanism that investigated incidents remotely from neighbouring countries, relied on questionable second-hand evidence and materials supplied by terrorist groups and dubious organizations like the White Helmets, and refused to visit the actual sites of alleged chemical incidents, including Khan Sheikhoun and the Shayrat airbase. When we demanded that the Mechanism conduct genuine, comprehensive, on-site investigations in accordance with basic international standards, our proposals were dismissed out of hand. 

Now we are accused of destroying the non-proliferation regime. This comes from delegations whose countries bear direct responsibility for destabilizing the entire Middle East, and from the United States, which, unlike the Russian Federation, has yet to destroy its own declared chemical weapons arsenals. 

Russia remains fully committed to the non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, the Chemical Weapons Convention, and the fight against impunity for chemical crimes. But we will not rubber-stamp flawed instruments designed merely to ratify predetermined political verdicts. If our Western partners genuinely valued the JIM and the unity of this Council, they would have engaged in honest, professional work instead of pursuing confrontation and cheap theatrical effects.
after.Sweden:
Mr. President,

Sweden voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Japan (S/2017/970). We want to express our sincere appreciation to the Japanese delegation for its tireless, constructive efforts over the past 24 hours to find common ground and bridge the divisions among Council members.

The proposal before us was a reasonable compromise: a technical rollover of 30 days that would have preserved the Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM) while giving the Council the necessary space and time to engage in substantive discussions on its future working methods, based on proposals from the Secretary-General. 

We are therefore deeply disappointed that, once again, a veto has prevented the Council from acting responsibly. The failure to extend the mandate of the JIM, an independent and professional body unanimously established by this Council, delivers a severe blow to the international disarmament and non-proliferation architecture. More critically, it sends an unacceptable message to the victims of chemical weapons attacks in Syria and threatens to entrench impunity.

The use of chemical weapons is a war crime and a grave threat to international peace and security. Ensuring accountability for these abhorrent acts is a core duty of the Security Council, not a geopolitical bargaining chip. 

Despite today’s deeply regrettable outcome, Sweden’s commitment to accountability remains steadfast. We will continue to support all efforts to ensure that the use of chemical weapons is never normalized and that those responsible for these heinous crimes are held to account.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
I thank the delegation of Japan for its tireless efforts over the past 24 hours to find a path forward and preserve the unity of this Council. Japan presented us with a sensible, constructive, and neutral proposal: a 30-day technical rollover to allow Council members the time and space to bridge differences and agree on the way forward for the Joint Investigative Mechanism (JIM). 

Twelve members of this Council voted in favour of that proposal today. That is an overwhelming majority, demonstrating the clear conviction of the Council that the use of chemical weapons cannot be tolerated and that those responsible must be held to account. 

Yet once again, Russia has abused its veto to block the will of the majority. This is the eleventh time Russia has used its veto to protect the Syrian regime, and the second time in less than twenty-four hours that it has used its veto to kill the JIM. 

Let us be completely clear about what has happened. Russia did not veto this resolution because of methodology or professional standards. Russia vetoed this resolution because the JIM dared to tell the truth. As long as the JIM pointed the finger at Da’esh, Russia was content. But the moment the JIM’s independent and professional experts concluded that the Syrian regime was responsible for horrific chemical attacks against its own people—most recently at Khan Shaykhun—Russia decided the Mechanism had to be eliminated. 

By killing the JIM, Russia has chosen to protect an ally that uses horrific weapons of mass destruction against civilians, rather than uphold the international non-proliferation architecture that has kept the world safe for decades. Russia has dealt a severe blow to the Chemical Weapons Convention and undermined the credibility of this Council.

To our Russian colleagues, I say: you may have killed the Joint Investigative Mechanism today, but you cannot kill the truth. You cannot hide the atrocities committed by the Assad regime. 

The United Kingdom, alongside our partners, will continue to work tirelessly to ensure that there is no impunity for the use of chemical weapons in Syria or anywhere else. Those who use these abhorrent weapons will be identified, and they will be held to account.
after.United States of America:
Russia has wasted our time. 

What we just saw today was not about the process. It was not about politics. It was not about compromise, and it was certainly not about the text of the resolution. Russia was never going to agree to any text that preserved an independent mechanism to investigate the use of chemical weapons in Syria. It was never going to agree to any mechanism that could shine a light on the use of chemical weapons by its ally, the Syrian regime. It is as simple as that.

I want to thank the delegation of Japan for its constructive, tireless efforts to find a compromise and give this Council one more opportunity to maintain the Joint Investigative Mechanism. Japan worked in good faith. A vast majority of the members of this Council voted in favor of this resolution, demonstrating once again the international community’s overwhelming desire to hold perpetrators of chemical weapons attacks accountable.

For the second time in 24 hours, and for the eleventh time on Syria, Russia has used its veto to protect the Assad regime. Russia has shown that it will stop at nothing to shield Assad from the consequences of using chemical weapons against his own people, even if it means destroying a mechanism that Russia itself helped create. 

Russia’s actions today and over these past weeks have been designed to delay, distract, and ultimately destroy the JIM. By killing the JIM, Russia has sent a dangerous message to the world: that impunity reigns, that the international norm against the use of chemical weapons can be violated with total disregard, and that Russia will use its veto to shield anyone who uses these horrific weapons.

The United States will not accept this. Even though Russia has single-handedly killed the JIM, our commitment to accountability will not waver. We will continue to work with our allies and partners to pursue justice for the victims of chemical attacks in Syria and to ensure that those who use these barbarous weapons are held accountable.
